title: PM Modi Tells Youth to Read Autobiographies, Warns Against Shortcut Culture at Kovind Book Launch
excerpt: At the release of former President Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography, Modi urged young people to find inspiration in real life stories instead of social media reels, saying "shortcuts will cut you short."
body:
• PM Modi launched former President Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography chronicling his journey from a modest upbringing to India's highest constitutional office.
  • Modi warned young people against the "shortcut culture" of reels and social media, telling them "shortcuts will cut you short."
  • He urged Gen-Z to read autobiographies for authentic life lessons rather than relying on short-form content.
  • Modi also shared a personal moment, remembering his late mother and saying he still feels the void of her absence.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the launch of former President Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography to deliver a pointed message to young Indians: put down the phone and pick up a book.

Speaking at the event, Modi praised Kovind's life journey — from a modest background to serving as India's 14th President from 2017 to 2022 — and urged youth to draw inspiration from autobiographies rather than the shortcut culture of social media reels.

A Warning Against Shortcuts

"Shortcuts will cut you short," Modi told the audience, a line that quickly circulated on social media. The prime minister cautioned young people against relying on reels and short-form content for life guidance, arguing that the depth of real experience found in autobiographies offers lessons that social media cannot.

Modi has previously addressed similar themes during his annual Pariksha Pe Charcha interactions with students, where he has spoken about the dangers of excessive screen time and the value of sustained reading and reflection.

Kovind's Journey

The newly released autobiography chronicles Kovind's remarkable trajectory. Born into a Dalit family in Uttar Pradesh's Kanpur Dehat district, he overcame significant social and economic barriers to become a lawyer, politician, and eventually India's president. His presidency from 2017 to 2022 was notable for its ceremonial significance as only the second Dalit to hold the office after K.R. Narayanan.

Modi praised the book as an example of the kind of story young people should seek out — one that demonstrates perseverance, hard work, and the value of education over quick fixes.

A Personal Moment

In an emotional aside, Modi spoke about his late mother, telling the audience that even today he feels the void of her absence. The personal reflection added an intimate dimension to an event that was otherwise focused on public messaging about education and self-improvement.

The moment drew attention on social media, with commentators noting that Modi rarely speaks publicly about his family in such direct terms.

The Bigger Picture

Modi's remarks come at a time when concerns about social media's impact on young people are growing globally. In India, where smartphone penetration among youth is among the highest in the world, the debate over screen time versus productive learning has intensified.

The prime minister's message also aligns with his government's broader push for reading and literacy. India's Young Authors Mentoring Scheme (YUVA) and the National Reading Day celebrations are part of ongoing efforts to promote book culture among young Indians.

For the Indian diaspora, Modi's emphasis on reading and self-improvement resonates with families who often prioritize education and intellectual development. Kovind's story of rising from a marginalized background to the presidency carries particular weight in communities that value upward mobility through hard work and learning.
nri_angle: Modi's message against shortcut culture and emphasis on reading resonates with diaspora families who value education and self-improvement, while Kovind's journey from a marginalized background to India's presidency is a story that inspires communities worldwide.
